title: docs(spec): ISecurityService TSDoc still says a context with no principal is admitted or keeps its scope; PR #22297 (#21908, ADR-0096 D5 strict mode) refuses it
body:
Filing gate: **① a contract text that the runtime no longer honours, once objectstack-ai/objectstack#22297 lands.** reach: the published `.d.ts` of `@objectstack/spec`. Every consumer that reads `ISecurityService`'s TSDoc is told the opposite of what the security plugin does.

Found by objectstack-ai/objectstack#21908's deny-round dev (`os-dev-report` `6060614288`, `open_questions[0]`). Filed by `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021), `session_01WkL6Eijt432S1Y7ekb6ovQ`. ⛔ Not graded or routed here; ⛔ not a claim.

Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#22297

## What is stale (`origin/main` `58707166`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`)

Each of these sentences describes the principal-less hand-off that #21908's deny removes:
- `getReadFilter` (near `:314-318`): "a context that carries no principal at all keeps the scope the other layers compose for it (ADR-0096 stages that context separately)".
- `canExport` (near `:628-631`): "only a context that carries no principal at all is admitted, as the middleware hands it through (ADR-0096)".
- `canReadObject` (near `:651-652`, the verdict's arm list): "only a context that carries no principal at all is handed through".
- `canReadObject` (near `:668-671`): "only a context that carries no principal at all is admitted, as the middleware hands it through (ADR-0096)".

After PR #22297, a context that carries no principal and is not a system context gets these answers:
- `canReadObject`, `canWriteObject` and `canExport` answer `false`;
- `getReadFilter` answers the deny filter;
- the engine middleware refuses every verb with `PermissionDeniedError` (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`);
- the field projections answer it as they answer any caller that resolves no permission set.

## A second stale text, found by PR #22297's contract review (`6061293231`)

`content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx` (near `:125-128`, the `ExecutionContext` passage) tells authors that "an automation run with no resolvable identity passes only its run id (`{ flowRunId }`), a context that deliberately carries no principal". After PR #22297, that context is refused with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. The sentence should state the refusal, and the two contexts that are admitted: the caller's own context, or the explicit system opt-in (`isSystem: true`). This is docs-only, outside `packages/spec`, and it belongs to the same release. Triage may route it with this card or as a sibling.

## Direction (for triage)

Correct the four sentences (three methods) to the deny, citing ADR-0096 D5 and its dated note (PR #22298, Tier H). Docs-only, in `packages/spec`, so it is spec-lane work.
- ⛔ No shape change.
- Land it right after PR #22297, in the same release, so the published contract and the runtime agree. That is why this card is blocked by the PR rather than folded into it: the `domain:services` claim does not hold `packages/spec`.

Dedupe: the four sentences' own words ("carries no principal at all is admitted") are the search key; this card is the first to name them.

Dedupe words: ISecurityService principal-less TSDoc · security-service.ts hand-off prose · strict mode spec contract text
